$comment: The kit's ONE default remote layout (ADR-001 amendments 9, 13): one root on the server; one directory per project under it; one disjoint tree per environment inside it; inside an environment, one directory per tier (catalogs.tiers: backend, frontend) holding one unit per service, and the stack's own configuration. A unit holds releases/<id> (one per packaged commit), `current` (the pointer a deploy and a rollback move), logs/ and runtime/ (the runtime config, mounted read-only), and in an environment with a workspace, workspace/ (remote dev). stack/ holds the environment's one compose file, each service's env file and the state of its units (which run their workspace); infra/ the environment's infra stack; backups/ what a backup of the environment writes. A target overrides any template (`layout`). Value placeholders: {root}, {project} (the project slug), {environment}, {tier} (the service's, from its role), {service}, {infraSlug}; `{@kind}` is another template of this file. Every rendered path must lie under `project`, and `project` strictly under the root: the root is shared between projects and never acted on. `unproven` is the one thing this layout's delivery may still say it lacks.
unproven: The release delivery (releases, current, rollback, the stack compose, runtime config) is proven with a recording transport and an in-memory server, not yet against a real docker host.
